\begin{abstract}
\noindent We run the released Jacobian-lens evaluations (6 sets) and
experiment prompt sets (11 sets) from the public companion release of
``Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language
Models'' under one audited harness on two open-weight models, and
separate prompt, lens, intervention, capability, and model effects.
This report covers the Qwen lane: the campaign-pinned checkpoint with
the published $n{=}1000$ lens --- the study's mechanical instrument
anchor (OR-Q1) and its first generalization surface (OR-Q2). Fidelity
classes and gate states are carried on every cell; gated cells are
missing, never zero; no confirmatory language is licensed anywhere in
Study 1.
\end{abstract}

\section{Qwen causal core (OR-Q2)}

\subsection{Verbal report}
\textbf{Incident note (or1-001):} the v1 numbers below score the
leading-space token form at a boundary whose in-context form is bare;
they \emph{understate} the effect (e.g.\ the \texttt{color:Red} swap
made the model's top-1 literally \texttt{Red} while the scored
\texttt{\textvisiblespace Red} form sat at rank 5). A v2 rerun with
min-over-forms scoring supersedes these at the next Qwen GPU slot; see
\texttt{reports/INCIDENT\_or1-001\_vr\_token\_form.md}.

Release-literal rule (first ten listed candidates, skip the answer),
swap-out = greedy token at the generation boundary (D1), $\alpha{=}1$
across the band at every prompt position. Category-equal top-1
\qwvrcattopone{} and top-5 \qwvrcattopfive{} over \qwvrncat{} categories
(\qwvrnexec{} executed trials; \qwvrimproved{} trials improved the
candidate's rank, \qwvrworsened{} worsened). Paper context (Claude):
88\% top-5. The effect on Qwen under the paper-literal operation is
\emph{directionally present in rank movement but far below the paper's
report-rate}: Fig.~\ref{fig:vr}.

\section{Worked examples: what the swaps actually do}

The aggregate rates hide a bimodal reality worth seeing item by item.
When the paper-literal swap works on Qwen, it works emphatically — the
predicted counterfactual answer jumps hundreds of ranks to top-1:

\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\qwpswinstable
\caption{The \qwpsnwins{} probe-swap successes (of 63 baseline-capable
items), largest baseline distance first. \texttt{ex2-city-capital-Munich}:
swapping the J-lens vector Munich$\to$(released target) at every prompt
position moves the predicted capital from rank 122 to the model's
literal output. One success (\texttt{rhyme-rain-neighbor}) was already
rank 1 before the swap (\qwpsnwinstrivial{} such trivial cell in the
count); \qwpsnnear{} further items land in the top-5 without reaching
top-1 — the modal failure is \emph{under-strength}, not wrong-direction.}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\qwfgwinstable
\caption{The \qwfgnwins{} flexible-generalization $\alpha{=}1$ successes
concentrate in the \emph{countries} category (capable top-1 23.3\%
there): \texttt{capital Egypt$\to$Canada} drives \texttt{Ottawa} from
rank 480 to the output. Months and numbers show none — the four
released categories differ enormously, exactly the per-category
variance the paper's own appendix warns about.}
\end{table}

Two structural observations. First, successes cluster where the
swapped-in argument has a strong, single-token, high-frequency identity
(cities, countries, elements); the sparse-identity categories (months
as time-words, small numbers) never flip. Second, the near-miss mass
(top-5 but not top-1) plus the incident-or1-001 form effect mean the
honest Qwen picture is ``the mechanism visibly engages but rarely
completes the flip at $\alpha{=}1$'' — which makes the $\alpha{=}2$
\emph{reversal} (0\% capable) the more interesting anomaly: on Qwen the
doubled patch overshoots into off-distribution territory rather than
completing near-misses, unlike the paper's Sonnet where $\alpha{=}2$
lifted 76/192 to 101/192.

\section{OR1-B: the OLMo official-estimator fit}

Timing gate (frozen before any outcome): dim\_batch ladder
161/164/181/232/386\,s per prompt for 16/8/4/2/1 $\Rightarrow$
dim\_batch=\olfitdimbatch{} at \olfitsperprompt{}\,s/prompt; only the
2$\times$125 tier fits the 18\,GPU-hour ceiling $\Rightarrow$ merged
$n{=}\olfitmerged$ (the addendum's honest-prior tier). Both halves
completed 125/125 with zero skips. Split-half operator audit: median
symmetric relative Frobenius \olshmedfrob{} across the 32 fitted layers
(\olshbandfrob{} in-band); minus-identity cosines $\approx$1.0
(fp32-accumulation readings marginally above 1 are numerical); late
layers are near-identity (identity fraction 0.93--0.97), so their
low top-64 subspace overlaps reflect noise-dominated residuals, not
disagreement. Readout stability: half-A/half-B eval pass@20 gaps
$\le$0.015 on every set --- far inside the 0.10 margin. \textbf{No
FIT-SENSITIVE classification; the merged lens is the OLMo primary.}

\subsection{OLMo causal core (v2 scoring throughout)}

\textbf{Verbal report}: category-equal top-1 \olvrcattopone{}, top-5
\olvrcattopfive{} (\olvrnexec{} executed; \olvrimproved{} improved /
\olvrworsened{} worsened). This is an order of magnitude above Qwen's
v1 numbers (v2 rerun pending) though far below the paper's 88\%
(Claude). \textbf{Flexible generalization}: capable top-1
\olfgcapaone{} ($\alpha{=}1$) $\to$ \olfgcapatwo{} ($\alpha{=}2$) ---
numerically indistinguishable from Qwen (5.8\%/0.0\%), \emph{including
the $\alpha{=}2$ reversal}: the over-strength overshoot is a
cross-model regularity of the paper-literal swap on open models,
whereas Sonnet 4.5 improved 76/192$\to$101/192. \textbf{Probe-swap raw
arm}: capable top-1 \olpscaptopone{} (diagnostic \olpsdiagtopone{};
\olpsncap{} capable of 90; paper 60\%).

\section{Interpretation under the wording router (two lanes)}

Conformance and admission passed mechanically on both lanes (exact
parity, exact no-ops, verified pins; fit stability inside every
margin), so all results above are scientific observations about
model/instrument cells, not harness states.

The two lanes \textbf{dissociate the readout and intervention
properties}. On Qwen the J-lens readout advantage reproduces exactly as
the paper describes (multihop/multilingual profiles), yet paper-literal
swaps barely move behavior. On OLMo the readout advantage largely
\emph{disappears} (logit lens already strong in-band; near-identity
$J_\ell$), yet verbal report shows the strongest open-model swap effect
so far (25.5\% top-5). Meanwhile flexible generalization behaves
identically on both lanes ($\approx$5\% capable at $\alpha{=}1$, 0\% at
$\alpha{=}2$) --- the $\alpha{=}2$ reversal is a shared open-model
regularity that inverts the paper's Sonnet finding. The g-folding
asymmetry (material on Qwen, immaterial on OLMo) marks a concrete
basis-choice difference between the campaign's instruments and the
paper's, live on exactly the lane where interventions are weakest.

Maximum licensed sentences at this boundary: for Qwen, the plan \S7.6
route \emph{``conformance passes, core null/mixed --- a valid Qwen
generalization result''}; for OLMo, a property-specific version of
Route~A's weaker half: verbal report is directionally present at
development tier, flexible generalization is not, and no
workspace-existence or -absence claim is licensed for either model.
The extended battery and the instrument cross-over (separating prompt,
lens, and intervention semantics --- OR-Q4) complete the picture in
OR1-D.
